overnightRisk: Three specific things between now and the ~02:00 COT midnight report. ONE - the 79,688.6 session low sits only 210.1 points under spot and the 79,750 bucket just above it absorbed 273,556 USD of liquidations today, so it is a proven battleground rather than clean air; a weekend book with 2,245 BTC of 24h spot volume - roughly a third of a normal weekday - can travel that distance on very little size. TWO - the short-covering fuel is spent. 91.3 percent of the 1,910,792 USD liquidated in the last 22.0 hours was SHORT and the 80,000 bucket alone consumed 1,210,000 USD of it, which means the sellers who were forced to buy have already bought. Funding has decayed to -0.0000204 percent, effectively flat, so nobody is being paid to hold either side into the gap. With the OKX long/short account ratio at 1.10, the crowded side by head count is now LONG, and the only untested pocket is the 262,140 USD of shorts at 80,250 - a magnet that needs a catalyst nobody is scheduled to provide before Monday. THREE - no macro release can help. US equity and ETF channels are closed until Monday, so Friday's +174.6m Farside row is the last confirmed flow print and there is no session to extend the three-day inflow streak; the 4H and daily MACD histograms are both negative and widening (-76.58 from -75.01, and -109.20 from -49.66) into that vacuum. The resting stop at 79,620 is deliberately set 50 points INSIDE the 79,570 confirmation gate: overnight I would rather be taken out by a wick I cannot watch than wait for a settled close I will not see.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull downgraded from UP to BALANCED, and the reason is the whole story of this session. Midday read the pull as up because the 80,250 short pocket was untested and the 80,000 shelf was being eaten; both are still true, but price tried 80,197.6, failed 52.4 points short of the pocket, and settled back UNDER 80,000. A magnet you reach and bounce off is a ceiling. Below, the 79,750 bucket is the most two-sided on the map, so there is no clean vacuum either way. The account ratio at 1.10 means the crowded side by head count is now long.

calibration.rollingRecord: Settled-close gates: 18 correct out of the last 19 evaluated sessions. BOTH midday gates resolved correctly and both by refusing to arm. The 79,620.0 reduce gate did not fire - the lowest low since was 79,688.6, a 68.6-point miss, and the lowest settled hourly close was 79,742.5, a further 122.5 points clear. The 80,325.0 add gate did not arm - the high was 80,197.6, 127.4 points short, and the highest settled close was 80,001.1. That is seven consecutive sessions in which a gate placed roughly 0.5 hourly ATRs beyond a proven wick has resolved correctly. The single failure in the window remains the 03 September midday add gate placed below an untested high.
calibration.note: The gates were right and the trade is red, and the two facts are not in conflict - they are the lesson. Midday honoured an armed morning gate by opening a 54 USDT 3x long at 80,040.1; price is 141.4 points below that entry, so acting cost roughly 0.10 USDT of unrealised on the futures leg while the spot core lost about 0.31 USDT on the drift. actingHelped is recorded FALSE. What midday got right was the caution it wrote down and then partly ignored in sizing: open interest was FALLING while price rose and the account ratio was climbing, which it correctly named as covering with retail arriving late. That is exactly how it played out - the covering finished, funding decayed from -0.00143 percent to -0.0000204 percent, the 80,250 pocket was never reached, and the move round-tripped. The process fix is not to refuse the gate; it is to treat a rally on flat-to-falling open interest as a scalp rather than a swing, and to size and hold it accordingly. Hence the halving into the gap rather than a full exit.
